page: Hetzner Cloud cax21 is an entry-tier ARM64 virtual server situated within the provider's Cost Optimized family, provisioned via the QEMU hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Ampere Altra processor featuring the Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. It supplies 4 shared vCPUs running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, operating with 1 thread per physical core and hardware AES cryptographic acceleration. System memory is sized at 8.0 GB, which equals approximately 1.95 GB of RAM per core. The server configuration includes 80 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage, while dedicated GPU hardware accelerators and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are absent.

Performance benchmarks show average throughput in compute and data handling routines alongside lower scores in intensive execution tasks. In stress-ng testing, the cax21 delivers 1777.99 single-core and 7055.54 multi-core scores, placing it in the middle tier of evaluated servers. Passmark database operations and uncached 256 MB memory bandwidth metrics also reflect middle-tier stability, achieving 45.11 GB/sec read and 26.08 GB/sec write rates. Conversely, single-core and multi-core Geekbench measurements, Clang compilation, and ray tracing fall within the bottom quartile. Redis SET operations achieve 4.44 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 4.52 GB/sec. LLM inference with a 135M parameter model reaches 169.73 prompt processing tokens per second and 46.26 generation tokens per second.

From an infrastructure standpoint, the cax21 provides favorable resource density by pairing four 64-bit ARM cores with fast NVMe storage under a shared-CPU model. The primary operational tradeoff involves shared core contention and moderate single-thread execution speed, making it less viable for compute-heavy compilation or high-frequency processing. The hardware profile and 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio render it appropriate for development environments, lightweight web servers, microservices, continuous integration runners, and non-critical backend tasks.
